INTEGRATED SCIENCE — PREMIUM EXAM 3
====

EXAM BODY: KJSEA
GRADE: Grade 8 JSS
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100

INSTRUCTIONS
----
• Answer all questions.
• For calculations, show full working (formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units).
• Diagrams provided are part of the question — use every labeled value.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In osmosis, what mainly moves across a selectively permeable membrane? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Sand grains
   C. Whole sugar crystals only
   D. Electric current

2. Eyepiece ×5 and objective ×40. What is total magnification? (1 mark)
   A. ×200
   B. ×45
   C. ×5
   D. ×80

3. Calculate pressure when F = 140 N and A = 0.4 m². (1 mark)
   A. 350 Pa
   B. 56 Pa
   C. 140.4 Pa
   D. 0.002857142857142857 Pa

[DIAGRAM]
TYPE: svg
PURPOSE: Show force F = 140 N acting on area A = 0.4 m² with P = F/A labeled.
ALT: Force arrow of 140 newtons pressing on a rectangular area of 0.4 square metres.
PAYLOAD:

  <text x="160" y="135" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" fill="#1b5e20">A = 0.4 m²</text>
  <line x1="160" y1="30" x2="160" y2="105" stroke="#b71c1c" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#arrow)"/>
  <defs><marker id="arrow" markerWidth="8" markerHeight="8" refX="4" refY="4" orient="auto"><path d="M0,0 L8,4 L0,8 Z" fill="#b71c1c"/></marker></defs>
  <text x="175" y="60" font-size="14" fill="#b71c1c">F = 140 N</text>
  <text x="160" y="170" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13" fill="#333">P = F / A</text>
</svg>
CAPTION: Figure 1: Force on an area for pressure
[/DIAGRAM]

4. The main energy chain in a simple torch is: (1 mark)
   A. Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)
   B. Light → chemical → sound
   C. Sound → nuclear → light
   D. Heat → food → electricity only

5. Iron has symbol Fe from the Latin name: (1 mark)
   A. Ferrum
   B. Natrium
   C. Aurum
   D. Kalium

6. Which statement correctly defines an element? (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical or physical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A substance that always conducts electricity

7. A learner writes calcium as CA. What is the correct symbol and rule? (1 mark)
   A. Ca — first letter capital, second letter small
   B. CA — both letters must be capitals
   C. ca — both letters must be small
   D. C — calcium uses only one letter

8. Why is table salt (NaCl) classified as a compound? (1 mark)
   A. It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio
   B. It is white and looks pure
   C. It melts when heated
   D. It is mined at Lake Magadi only

9. Which change is physical? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Baking soda reacting with vinegar to make a new gas

10. Which property of liquids is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Definite volume, no definite shape
   B. Definite shape and definite volume
   C. No definite volume and no mass
   D. Always denser than every solid

11. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread the burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water removes heat too quickly

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. Correct option: A — Water

2. Correct option: A — ×200
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective
2. Substitute values: Total = 5 × 40
3. Total = 200
Final Answer: ×200
Marks: M1 multiply; A1 answer

3. Correct option: A — 350 Pa
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: P = F / A
2. Substitute values: P = 140 / 0.4
3. P = 350
Final Answer: 350 Pa
Marks: M1 substitute; A1 Pa

4. Correct option: A — Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)

5. Correct option: A — Ferrum

6. Correct option: A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical or physical means

7. Correct option: A — Ca — first letter capital, second letter small

8. Correct option: A — It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio

9. Correct option: A — Ice melting to water

10. Correct option: A — Definite volume, no definite shape

11. Correct option: A — Water can spread the burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

12. Correct option: A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

13. Correct option: A — Water

14. Correct option: A — ×200
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: Total magnification = eyepiece × objective
2. Substitute values: Total = 5 × 40
3. Total = 200
Final Answer: ×200
Marks: M1 multiply; A1 answer

15. Correct option: A — 350 Pa
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: P = F / A
2. Substitute values: P = 140 / 0.4
3. P = 350
Final Answer: 350 Pa
Marks: M1 substitute; A1 Pa

16. Correct option: A — Chemical → electrical → light (+ heat)

17. Correct option: A — Ferrum

18. Correct option: A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical or physical means

19. Correct option: A — Ca — first letter capital, second letter small

20. Correct option: A — It contains sodium and chlorine chemically joined in a fixed ratio

21. Correct option: A — Ice melting to water

22. Correct option: A — Definite volume, no definite shape

23. Correct option: A — Water can spread the burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

24. (5 marks)
Chemical energy (cells) → electrical energy (circuit) → light energy + heat energy (bulb).

25. (5 marks)
An element is a pure substance of one kind of atom and cannot be broken down chemically/physically into simpler substances (e.g. copper in wires, Fe in a jembe). A compound is made when different elements join chemically in fixed proportions (e.g. NaCl table salt, H₂O).

26. (6 marks)
Melting ice: still H₂O, no new substance, reversible by freezing → physical. Burning paper: ash/gases form, new substances, not simply reversible → chemical.

27. (8 marks)
Working:
1. Formula / relationship: P = F / A
2. Substitute values: P = 170 / 0.5
3. P = 340
Final Answer: 340 Pa
Marks: M1 formula/substitution; A1 final answer with Pa

28. (6 marks)
Fuel, heat, oxygen. For oil fires, do not use water; smother/cover to cut oxygen and get help / evacuate if needed.

29. (6 marks)
Osmosis: water moves across a selectively permeable membrane from dilute toward more concentrated solution. Water enters the tubing; it swells/gains mass.

30. (5 marks)
Chemical energy (cells) → electrical energy (circuit) → light energy + heat energy (bulb).

31. (5 marks)
An element is a pure substance of one kind of atom and cannot be broken down chemically/physically into simpler substances (e.g. copper in wires, Fe in a jembe). A compound is made when different elements join chemically in fixed proportions (e.g. NaCl table salt, H₂O).
